data.title: Grayscale Names Robinhood Chain, BNB Chain And Solana As Tokenized Stock Winners
data.description: Grayscale said Robinhood Chain, BNB Chain and Solana handled most tokenized stock trading last week, with weekly spot volume for the sector peaking near $3 billion in early August. According to BeInCrypto, the note said only about 5% of the tokenized equity market is used in on-chain finance, while value locked in tokenized stocks passed $110 million in late August. Grayscale also said lending is starting to catch up, with holdings inside Kamino and Jupiter growing roughly tenfold in a year.

data.title: Nepal Floods Damage Hydropower Plants And Cut Power Capacity
data.description:
According to the BBC, deadly floods in Nepal last Wednesday severely damaged 12 hydropower plants in the Trishuli River basin and knocked out more than 10% of the country's total power generation capacity. Operators said they do not yet know whether any of the facilities can be restored, while the state-owned Nepal Electricity Authority said supply remains adequate for households.

The floods destroyed entire villages near the border with Tibet and killed more than 1,300 people, with thousands still missing. Nepal relies on hydropower for almost all of its electricity and earns nearly $200m a year exporting power to India and Bangladesh, but officials and energy experts said the disaster highlights the need to rethink the country's hydropower strategy and diversify into other sources such as solar and wind. The Upper Trishuli-1 project, one of Nepal's largest foreign direct investment ventures at about $647m, was among the worst hit, and insurers have paid around $40m for flood-related damage to more than 20 privately owned plants over the past three years.

data.title: U.S. Judge Extends Block on New Mail Voting Rules
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, a U.S. judge on September 4 extended the restriction on new mail voting rules for the U.S. government, after Boston federal district judge Indira Talwani issued a 14-day temporary restraining order on August 27 night that paused the U.S. Postal Service from enforcing the rules and set a hearing for September 3 on whether to impose a longer-term injunction. The U.S. government appealed on August 28.

data.title: BitFuFu Adds 59 Bitcoin, Raises Holdings to 1,373 BTC
data.description: BitcoinTreasuries.NET said on X that Singapore-listed Bitcoin mining company BitFuFu has added 59 Bitcoin to its holdings, bringing its total to 1,373 BTC. According to Odaily, BitFuFu ranks 39th in the Bitcoin 100 list.

data.title: STOCKS | X Wins Early Ruling Blocking Use of Twitter-Related Trademarks
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, X won an early lawsuit ruling blocking a company from using some trademarks related to Twitter after U.S. District Judge Colm F. Connolly in Delaware ruled on Thursday that Operation Bluebird's defense claiming X had abandoned eight trademarks containing Twitter elements failed.

data.title: AI Boosts Cybersecurity Demand at Zscaler, Jay Chaudhry Says
data.description:
Zscaler Chief Executive Officer Jay Chaudhry said AI is increasing demand for cybersecurity rather than reducing the need for software security, according to Bloomberg.

He said CEOs, CIOs and boards want to use AI for productivity and cost savings, but worry new AI models could create vulnerabilities, lead to breaches or leave applications exposed to hacking or hijacking.

data.title: KPMG's Diane Swonk Sees Mixed Signals in August Jobs Report
data.description:
Diane Swonk, chief economist at KPMG, said the August jobs report showed mixed but strong labor market signals, according to Bloomberg. U.S. payrolls rose by 162,000, above expectations, while the unemployment rate held at 4.1%.

The report also included revisions to prior figures, and Swonk said the data contain a lot of noise.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | FDA Approves AstraZeneca Breast Cancer Pill
data.description:
AstraZeneca Plc’s breast cancer pill won approval from the US Food and Drug Administration, according to Bloomberg.

The decision is a win for AstraZeneca after the agency’s advisory panel previously voted against the medicine.

data.title: G7 Cybersecurity Group Urges Immediate Migration to Post-Quantum Cryptography
data.description:
The G7 cybersecurity working group said in a new report that quantum computing poses both security and economic threats to public and private institutions, and organizations should begin migrating to post-quantum cryptography immediately. According to ChainCatcher, the group said the transition could take years, while attackers may already be collecting encrypted data now and waiting to decrypt it once sufficiently powerful quantum computers become available.

The report said quantum computing could also break digital signatures, enabling identity spoofing and exposing companies and their supply chains. It did not mention cryptocurrencies, but the same public-key cryptography is used for blockchain wallets and transaction authorization. Current quantum computers are not yet able to break Bitcoin cryptography, though developers are considering post-quantum proposals such as BIP-360. Ethereum researchers plan to replace several cryptographic components used by accounts, validators, and applications, while the Solana Foundation has tested post-quantum signatures on a testnet and introduced an optional hash-based vault. The G7 group also urged governments to support research, public-private cooperation, and national PQC strategies.

data.title: G7 Cybersecurity Group Urges Immediate Migration to Post-Quantum Cryptography
data.description:
The Group of Seven cybersecurity working group said in its latest report that quantum computing poses both security and economic threats to public and private institutions, and organizations should begin moving to post-quantum cryptography immediately. According to Odaily, the group said the migration could take years, while attackers can already collect and store encrypted data for later decryption once sufficiently powerful quantum computers emerge.

The report said quantum computing could also break digital signatures, enabling identity theft and exposing companies and their supply chains. It did not mention cryptocurrencies, but noted that similar public-key cryptography is used for blockchain wallets and transaction authorization.

The report said current quantum computers cannot break Bitcoin cryptography, though developers are considering post-quantum proposals such as BIP-360. Ethereum researchers plan to replace several cryptographic components used by accounts, validators, and applications, while the Solana Foundation has tested post-quantum signatures on a testnet and introduced an optional hash-based vault. The G7 working group also urged governments to support related research, public-private cooperation, and national PQC strategies.

data.title: US Market Roundup: Trump Threatens Tariffs, Volkswagen Seeks U.S. Revival, Citi Delays Fed Cut Outlook
data.description:
U.S. President Donald Trump said the United States could strike Iran’s nuclear facilities at Mount Fordow soon and urged the Federal Reserve to cut rates sharply or face a halt in trade with countries that run surpluses with the U.S.

According to Sina Finance, Volkswagen is trying to revive its U.S. business, while the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has opened an investigation into Tesla’s Cybercab project to determine whether it meets safety standards.

According to Sina Finance, Citi economists now expect the Federal Reserve to cut rates three times in 2027, each by 25 basis points, after stronger-than-expected August employment data.

According to Sina Finance, Federal Reserve official Beth M. Hammack said it is time to take action to lower inflation.

data.title: Novartis Heart Drug Misses Late-Stage Trial Goal
data.description: A Novartis AG drug billed as a potential blockbuster failed to cut the risk of heart attacks and strokes in a final-stage trial, according to Bloomberg. The result is a setback for the company’s new approach to preventing cardiovascular disease.

data.title: STOCKS | S&P Dow Jones Indices Adds Bloom Energy, Illumina, and Everpure to S&P 500
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, S&P Dow Jones Indices said it will add Bloom Energy, Illumina, and Everpure to the S&P 500 Index.

data.title: Argentina Survey Cuts 2026 GDP Growth Forecast to 2.1%, Raises Inflation Outlook to 30%
data.description: According to Jin10, Argentina's central bank market expectations survey showed that Argentina's GDP growth forecast for the end of 2026 was 2.1%, down 0.6 percentage points from the previous forecast, while the inflation forecast for the end of 2026 was 30%, up 0.21 percentage points from the previous forecast.

data.title: Polymarket Launches Perpetual Contracts for Bitcoin, Gold, and Major Indices
data.description:
Polymarket launched its Polymarket Perps product on September 3, initially offering 10 contracts covering Bitcoin, Ether, Solana, HYPE, gold, silver, WTI crude oil, the S&P 500, the Nasdaq 100, and contracts tracking SpaceX stock. According to Odaily, the product expanded to 67 markets within hours.

The contracts have no expiration date and track the underlying assets continuously, with hourly funding rates used to keep prices anchored to spot levels. The funding rate is capped at 4% per hour in both directions. Crypto assets, the S&P 500, crude oil, gold, and silver support leverage of up to 20 times, while individual stocks and other real-world assets support up to 10 times.

U.S. traders cannot place Perps orders and are redirected to Polymarket US, which is regulated by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. The arrangement stems from Polymarket's 2022 settlement with the CFTC, when the company was fined $1.4 million for operating an unregistered swap trading facility and was ordered to stop the noncompliant contracts.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Trump’s Venezuela Oil Deal Worries U.S. Executives
data.description:
US President Donald Trump’s broad oil deal with Venezuela, which he says effectively gives the United States control over much of the country’s oil wealth, has unsettled U.S. oil executives, according to Bloomberg.

Trump called it possibly "the best deal ever signed."

data.title: S&P Cuts Senegal Further Into Junk on Debt Restructuring Plan
data.description:
S&P Global Ratings lowered Senegal’s credit score further into junk territory after the government unveiled a plan to restructure its obligations, according to Bloomberg.

The ratings firm said a distressed debt exchange or default on Senegal’s foreign-currency commercial debt is "extremely likely."

data.title: Ricardo Salinas Pliego Says Bitcoin Could Reach $1.86 Million on Gold Parity
data.description: Mexican billionaire Ricardo Salinas Pliego renewed his long-term Bitcoin thesis, saying BTC could rise to $1.86 million per coin if it matches gold’s market value. According to BeInCrypto, the Grupo Salinas founder said Bitcoin’s adoption is still very early and reiterated that he sees BTC as superior digital gold. He also said his liquid portfolio is mostly in Bitcoin-related assets, often 70%-80%, with the rest split between gold and mining stocks.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Hedge Funds Raise Brent Bullish Bets to May High as US-Iran Fighting Intensifies
data.description: Hedge funds became the most bullish on Brent crude since May as fresh fighting between the US and Iran raised concerns about prolonged disruptions to energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: US Market Close | Stocks Fall as Treasury Yields Rise After Jobs Data
data.description:
U.S. stocks closed lower on Friday as Treasury yields rose after the jobs data was released, with the 2-year Treasury yield touching its highest level since January 2025. According to Sina Finance, CME FedWatch showed federal funds futures traders pricing a 58% chance of a Fed rate hike in two weeks, up from 49.4% the previous day.

The S&P 500 fell 0.38% to 7,718.60, the Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.29% to 26,506.99, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 271.86 points, or 0.51%, to 53,414.25. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose more than 3%, while memory stocks surged, with SanDisk up more than 11%, SK Hynix up more than 8%, Seagate Technology down more than 6%, Western Digital up more than 5%, and Micron Technology up more than 6%.

The August nonfarm payrolls report showed employment rose by 162,000, well above the 53,000 forecast in a Dow Jones survey of economists. The unemployment rate held at 4.1%, in line with market expectations, and June and July employment figures were both revised higher.

Juniper Henderson portfolio manager Bradford Smith said the August jobs report was very strong and reflected much greater volatility in labor data, while slightly increasing the odds of a September rate hike. He added that the debate over Fed policy would depend heavily on upcoming inflation data. Smith also said that after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivered a hawkish signal at Jackson Hole last week, the Fed had formed a clear bias toward raising rates if later data failed to show more progress on cooling inflation.

For the week, the Dow fell 0.3%, the S&P 500 rose 0.1%, and the Nasdaq Composite gained 0.4%.
